_comment: A crossing (W14, rebuilt W21). Local y = 0 is the deck's UNDERSIDE and the site is floored with ground:"water" (Settlements): the river's surface plus a clearance, or the bank if that is higher, so the deck is never in the water and never under the bank. The first build stood on terrain max under a footprint that lay wholly inside the cut, which is the riverbed -- the owner filmed the deck a few metres under the surface. The river's cut is 74 m across (90 m at the Wide Water), so the deck runs the full 90 m: 30 m of span on three piers in the channel and a 30 m causeway on a solid abutment either side, both reaching far below any bed. The two `approach` flights have no length written here: `reach: ground` makes StructureBuilder walk each one down from the deck end until it meets the bank, so a low bank gets a long stair and a high bank a short one. The river kills, so a bridge is not scenery -- it is the only way across.
name: river_bridge
